blocks.content: Abrasion acts as the main tool of river erosion, grinding sediment particles against the channel bed and banks like natural sandpaper.

rows: Physical force of water and compressed air

items: Do not confuse Corrasion (mechanical wear by rocks against the channel) with Corrosion (chemical dissolution of minerals).
Attrition reduces the load size itself, while Abrasion wears away the surrounding river channel.
Vertical erosion dominates the upper course to form V-shaped valleys, whereas lateral erosion dominates the middle course to widen the valley.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Hydraulic Action operates through the physical force of flowing water dislodging loose riverbed materials.
Abrasion (Corrasion) occurs when the river uses its load of rocks and sand as tools to scrape and grind the bed and banks.
Attrition involves rock fragments colliding with each other in the current, becoming smaller, smoother, and rounder over time.
Solution (Corrosion) is the chemical dissolving of soluble rock structures, particularly limestone and chalk, by slightly acidic water.
